ALIAS-SCOPE GUARD, APPLIED TO BOTH EDGES, AND IT IS THE FILE'S FIRST FINDING: the catalog alias for this identity is the literal string 'oral mucositis', which silently widens the identity to cancer-therapy-induced mucositis, a distinct clinical entity with its own literature, instruments and management. EVERY LOCATED ANCHOR ON THIS FILE studies one or the other of those two forms, and NOT stomatitis in general. Any claim must therefore document the AETIOLOGY, and no edge on this file may be applied to infectious, traumatic, nutritional or idiopathic stomatitis on the strength of this evidence.

AETIOLOGY-CONTRAST GUARD, APPLIED TO THE MOOD EDGE: the dysphagia anchors study TREATMENT-INDUCED disease, while two of the three mood anchors study RECURRENT APHTHOUS STOMATITIS, a different disease entity. The two aetiologies are deliberately kept side by side because the contrast is what makes the direction problem visible, and the aetiology difference is disclosed on the face of the edge rather than smoothed over.

DIRECTION GUARD, APPLIED TO THE MOOD EDGE: the only prospective longitudinal anchor found that the individuals who went on to develop mucositis ALREADY HAD HIGHER ANXIETY AND DEPRESSION SCORES AT BASELINE, before the lesion existed. The edge is therefore registered as direction-unresolved and the mechanism claim names BOTH arms of the loop, rather than authored as a consequence.

AGENT-SPECIFICITY GUARD, APPLIED TO THE DYSPHAGIA EDGE: the association is significant for CHEMOTHERAPY-induced mucositis and NOT significant for RADIOTHERAPY-induced mucositis in the same study on the same adjusted model, with a confidence interval of 0.84 to 1.77 crossing the null. Any claim MUST NAME THE INDUCING AGENT CLASS and may not generalise across it.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Dysphagia is the systemic consequence most consistently documented for the treatment-induced form of this identity, and the located evidence supplies both an adjusted odds ratio and a pooled prevalence, together with an internal null. A national-data study of 59,710 HOSPITALISED PATIENTS WITH CANCERS OF THE ORAL CAVITY, LIP AND PHARYNX and of 10,885 hospitalised hematopoietic stem cell transplant patients found that CHEMOTHERAPY-INDUCED ORAL ULCERATIVE MUCOSITIS WAS ASSOCIATED WITH A GREATER LIKELIHOOD OF DYSPHAGIA, adjusted odds ratio 2.11 (95% CI 1.52 to 2.95) in the head-and-neck group and 2.08 (95% CI 1.11 to 3.9) in transplant patients, and with increased length of stay, coefficients 1.54 (95% CI 1.36 to 1.74) and 1.09 (95% CI 1.02 to 1.16) respectively; the same study also found that mucositis outcomes DISPROPORTIONATELY AFFECT FEMALES, BLACKS, HISPANICS, MEDICAID RECIPIENTS AND THOSE WITH LOWER INCOMES (PMID 39666090). THE SAME STUDY REPORTS A NULL THAT IS CARRIED ON THIS EDGE: RADIOTHERAPY-INDUCED ORAL ULCERATIVE MUCOSITIS WAS ALSO associated with increased length of stay but showed NO ASSOCIATION WITH DYSPHAGIA (adjusted odds ratio 1.21, 95% CI 0.84 to 1.77) (PMID 39666090). A PRISMA systematic review and meta-analysis of 24 cross-sectional studies of oral manifestations in individuals undergoing chemotherapy pooled a DYSPHAGIA PREVALENCE OF 28.28 PERCENT, alongside oral mucositis at 42.15, dysgeusia at 49.62, gingivitis at 56.15, xerostomia at 39.92, oral ulcer at 31.40, candidiasis at 24.11, oral pain at 22.78, halitosis at 19.55 and oral herpes at 7.98 percent (PMID 41914550). Recorded as documented association only, with the radiotherapy null carried openly, and with the alias-scope problem set out below.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and THE ALIAS-SCOPE PROBLEM IS THE FIRST LIMITATION: the catalog alias for this identity is the literal string 'oral mucositis', which silently widens the identity to cancer-therapy-induced mucositis, a distinct clinical entity with its own literature, its own instruments and its own management. BOTH ANCHORS on this edge study TREATMENT-INDUCED disease and not stomatitis in general, so the edge is registered as a treatment-induced finding applied to an identity whose catalog alias merges the two, and that mapping is disclosed on the face of the edge rather than buried. A SECOND LIMITATION IS INTERNAL TO THE STRONGEST ANCHOR: the dysphagia association is significant for CHEMOTHERAPY-induced mucositis and NOT significant for RADIOTHERAPY-induced mucositis in the same study, on the same adjusted model, with a confidence interval from 0.84 to 1.77 crossing the null, so a claim that this identity causes dysphagia must name the inducing agent class and may not generalise across it. The pooled 28.28 percent is a PREVALENCE OF A MANIFESTATION IN A CHEMOTHERAPY POPULATION rather than a complication rate for this identity, and the review's own authors attribute the whole result set to CONSIDERABLE HETEROGENEITY AMONG THE STUDIES. The first anchor is a retrospective analysis of ADMINISTRATIVE DATA in which dysphagia is a coded outcome among hospitalised patients, so it captures dysphagia severe enough to be coded, and it reports the association in an inpatient population rather than an ambulatory one. Individual claims require a dated diagnosis with the AETIOLOGY documented, whether infectious, drug-induced, traumatic, nutritional or treatment-induced, a structured dysphagia assessment with the instrument and the consistency texture named, a nutritional status assessment with weight trajectory, a documented oncology treatment history where applicable, and a clinical determination separating direct mucosal pain from post-treatment oedema, from xerostagia-induced difficulty forming a bolus, from a pre-existing swallowing disorder and from a second independent cause of dysphagia.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is mechanical bolus failure driven by a destroyed mucosal surface: the oral mucosa that initiates the swallow and that coats the bolus with saliva is ulcerated, so the bolus is formed on a raw surface with no intact epithelium to withstand the shear of a swallow and no normal mucosal sensation to trigger the swallow reflex, and the resulting painful, uncoordinated swallow causes reduced intake, which worsens the mucosal condition, so the cycle is self-sustaining; the vector is named as this mechanical-and-painful mechanism rather than as an obstruction or a neurological one, because the located evidence measures a mucosal ulcerative lesion and a dysphagia association in the same population and never reports a mechanical obstruction.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at national-administrative-data-cohort and PRISMA-systematic-review-of-cross-sectional-studies class, following the file's existing dental, oral, oncological and swallowing pathway scope. The administrative-data study is the anchor that carries the edge because it is the only located source supplying an ADJUSTED ODDS RATIO, 2.11 and 2.08, which is what allows a claim to say the association survives adjustment rather than merely that the two co-occur, and its disparity finding is registered because an association that falls unequally is an association that a claim must not present as uniform (PMID 39666090). Its radiotherapy null is carried on the face of the edge and is the single most important qualification on it, since it means the dysphagia association is agent-specific within the same study on the same model (PMID 39666090). The meta-analysis is registered for breadth, pooling ten oral manifestations across 24 cross-sectional studies including a 28.28 percent dysphagia prevalence, and its considerable-heterogeneity caveat is disclosed (PMID 41914550). Because both anchors study treatment-induced disease rather than this identity in general, and because the pooled figure is a prevalence of a manifestation rather than a complication rate, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only and states no rate for stomatitis outside the treatment setting.

NO located anchor reports a dysphagia severity grade, a need for enteral or parenteral support, a weight-loss trajectory, an aspiration rate or a mortality attributable to dysphagia in this population, and none reports whether pre-emptive oral care alters the outcome.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Xerostagia-induced difficulty forming a bolus, which the meta-analysis pools as a separate manifestation at 39.92 percent in the same population and which produces dysphagia by a different mechanism in the same patients
Post-treatment oedema or fibrosis producing a mechanical obstruction, which is a different route and which the located evidence does not separate from direct mucosal pain

A pre-existing swallowing disorder or a second independent cause of dysphagia, which the administrative-data design cannot exclude and which the ambulatory population would contain at a different rate
Aspiration arising from impaired bolus control, which the located evidence does not measure at all, so an individual with this edge's dysmotility may be aspirating without any documented event

Dysphagia attributable to the underlying malignancy itself or to its surgical resection, which is the dominant alternative explanation in a head-and-neck cancer population and which the located study does not fully adjust for

sourceReferences.citation: Mohan MP, Pili R, Epstein JB, et al. Cancer treatment-induced ulcerative mucositis serves as a significant predictor of burden of illness including dysphagia, and associated disparities among hospitalized cancer patients. Support Care Cancer. 2024 Dec 12;33(1):22. doi: 10.1007/s00520-024-09071-4. PMID 39666090.
sourceReferences.note: NATIONAL-DATA STUDY USING GENERALIZED LINEAR MODELS to examine the association of CHEMOTHERAPY-INDUCED ORAL ULCERATIVE MUCOSITIS and RADIOTHERAPY-INDUCED ORAL ULCERATIVE MUCOSITIS with burden of illness measured as length of stay and dysphagia, among 820 patients with chemotherapy-induced and 1,010 with radiotherapy-induced mucositis drawn from 59,710 HOSPITALISED PATIENTS WITH CANCERS OF THE ORAL CAVITY, LIP AND PHARYNX, and 1,380 patients with chemotherapy-induced mucositis from 10,885 hospitalised hematopoietic stem cell transplant patients. CHEMOTHERAPY-INDUCED MUCOSITIS WAS ASSOCIATED WITH INCREASED LENGTH OF STAY, coefficient 1.54 (95% CI 1.36 to 1.74), AND WITH A GREATER LIKELIHOOD OF DYSPHAGIA, adjusted odds ratio 2.11 (95% CI 1.52 TO 2.95); among transplant patients, coefficient 1.09 (95% CI 1.02 to 1.16) and adjusted odds ratio 2.08 (95% CI 1.11 to 3.9). A NULL CARRIED ON THE EDGE: RADIOTHERAPY-INDUCED MUCOSITIS WAS ALSO ASSOCIATED WITH INCREASED LENGTH OF STAY, coefficient 1.33 (95% CI 1.14 to 1.55), BUT SHOWED NO ASSOCIATION WITH DYSPHAGIA, adjusted odds ratio 1.21 (95% CI 0.84 TO 1.77). The authors further report that mucositis outcomes DISPROPORTIONATELY AFFECT FEMALES, BLACKS, HISPANICS, MEDICAID RECIPIENTS AND THOSE WITH LOWER INCOMES, and conclude that more effective screening and prevention of mucositis is needed alongside mucositis prediction modelling. Registered as the only located adjusted odds ratio for this association, and for its internal null. DISCLOSED: RETROSPECTIVE ADMINISTRATIVE DATA IN AN INPATIENT POPULATION, so it captures coded dysphagia among hospitalised cancer patients rather than an ambulatory complication rate.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: Support Care Cancer. 2024;33(1):22. National-data study of 59,710 hospitalised head-and-neck cancer and 10,885 transplant patients: chemotherapy-induced oral ulcerative mucositis associated with dysphagia at adjusted odds ratio 2.11 (95% CI 1.52-2.95) and 2.08 (95% CI 1.11-3.9), while radiotherapy-induced mucositis showed no dysphagia association (1.21, 95% CI 0.84-1.77); mucositis outcomes disproportionately affected females, Black, Hispanic and Medicaid patients.

sourceReferences.note: PRISMA SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS, registered in PROSPERO as CRD42024564007, of 24 CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDIES evaluating oral manifestations associated with chemotherapy, with risk of bias assessed using the JBI Critical Appraisal tool. POOLED PREVALENCES WERE: ORAL MUCOSITIS 42.15 PERCENT, DYSGEUSIA 49.62 PERCENT, GINGIVITIS 56.15 PERCENT, XEROSTOMIA 39.92 PERCENT, ORAL ULCER 31.40 PERCENT, DYSPHAGIA 28.28 PERCENT, CANDIDIASIS 24.11 PERCENT, ORAL PAIN 22.78 PERCENT, HALITOSIS 19.55 PERCENT and ORAL HERPES 7.98 PERCENT. The authors conclude that the prevalence of oral manifestations is high in patients undergoing chemotherapy, but that THE RESULTS SHOULD BE INTERPRETED WITH CAUTION DUE TO THE CONSIDERABLE HETEROGENEITY AMONG THE STUDIES. Registered for breadth, pooling ten oral manifestations in one population, and specifically for the dysphagia figure. DISCLOSED: the 28.28 PERCENT IS A PREVALENCE OF A MANIFESTATION IN A CHEMOTHERAPY POPULATION rather than a complication rate for this identity, the review is of cross-sectional studies only, and the authors' own heterogeneity caveat is carried on the face of the edge.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Psychological distress is the most repeatedly reported accompaniment of this identity in the located literature, and the strongest anchor reverses the direction that the edge's own name would suggest. A prospective longitudinal study of 37 individuals receiving chemotherapy at a Brazilian referral service, assessed with the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, the WHOQOL-BREF and the Oral Health Impact Profile at baseline and at day 15, found that NEARLY 38 PERCENT DEVELOPED CHEMOTHERAPY-INDUCED ORAL MUCOSITIS AND HAD HIGHER ANXIETY AND DEPRESSION SCORES AT BASELINE, that is BEFORE the mucositis developed, and that oral mucositis had a negative impact on oral health-related quality of life regarding functional limitation, physical pain, physical disability and handicap (PMID 38154442). A cross-sectional study of patients with recurrent aphthous stomatitis found that PROLONGED ULCER DURATION and a preference for traditional Chinese medicine interventions were significant risk factors for ANXIOUS AND DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS, that LARGER ULCER DIAMETER (B EQUALS 2.09, p EQUALS 0.017) and HIGHER ULCER RECURRENCE FREQUENCY (B EQUALS 4.74, p LESS THAN 0.001) EXACERBATED DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS, and that worsening pain and frequent fried-food consumption were associated with poorer oral health-related quality of life (PMID 41234733). A cross-sectional study of patients with recurrent aphthous stomatitis found SIGNIFICANTLY HIGHER PREVALENCE of extreme stress at 31.5 percent, extreme anxiety at 66.1 PERCENT AND DEPRESSION AT 30.6 PERCENT compared with those without the oral condition, and pain severity correlating moderately with stress and anxiety at r EQUALS 0.65 and 0.60 and mildly with depression at r EQUALS 0.35 (PMID 39036205). Recorded as documented association only, with the direction reversal carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and THE DIRECTION IS REVERSED ON THE STRONGEST ANCHOR, which is the located finding and is stated first: the only prospective longitudinal anchor found that the patients who went on to develop mucositis ALREADY HAD HIGHER ANXIETY AND DEPRESSION SCORES AT BASELINE, BEFORE the mucositis existed, so on that evidence the mood symptoms preceded the oral lesion rather than following it, and this edge therefore registers an association whose direction the located prospective design points AGAINST its own name. That anchor is also a SINGLE-CENTRE SAMPLE OF 37 INDIVIDUALS with a median age of 49, in which mucositis occurred in roughly fourteen people, so its baseline finding rests on a small subgroup. The two recurrent-aphthous-stomatitis anchors study a DIFFERENT AETIOLOGY entirely, one of them not treatment-induced at all, and the aphthous form is a distinct disease entity which the located literature does not present as a severity variant of this identity; both are registered because the two aetiologies are exactly the contrast that makes the direction question visible, and both are disclosed as a different aetiology on the face of the edge. The 66.1 percent extreme-anxiety figure in the third anchor is extraordinarily high, is measured against patients WITHOUT the oral condition rather than against population norms, and comes from a study whose own analysis of psychological variables is presented as correlational. A further caution is carried: the second anchor's predictors include dietary preferences, and both of its aphthous anchors are cross-sectional, so they cannot order ulcer severity and mood. Individual claims require a dated diagnosis with the AETIOLOGY documented, whether treatment-induced, aphthous, herpetiform, traumatic, nutritional, drug-induced or idiopathic, a structured depression instrument administered and scored with the instrument and its threshold named, a baseline mood assessment predating the oral episode where the aetiology permits it, an oral pain and ulcer-severity scale with the instrument named, and a clinical determination separating a depressive disorder from a mood response to recurrent oral pain, from adjustment to visible oral disease, from anxiety about eating and from a pre-existing mood disorder.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is a pain-driven avoidance loop with a plausible reverse arm: recurrent oral ulceration produces pain on eating, the patient avoids the painful meals and narrows diet and social eating, reduced intake and social withdrawal lower mood, and low mood is then recorded on the same instruments as a depressive disorder; the located prospective anchor supplies the reverse arm, showing that people who were already more anxious and depressed before treatment were the ones who went on to develop mucositis, which is consistent with a stress-mediated susceptibility to the lesion rather than a purely consequence relationship, so the mechanism claim names BOTH arms and states that the located evidence cannot arbitrate between them.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at prospective-longitudinal-cohort, cross-sectional-cohort-with-regression and cross-sectional-correlational-study class, following the file's existing dental, oral and psychological pathway scope. The prospective cohort is the anchor that carries the edge AND the anchor that constrains it, because it is the only located source with a baseline mood measurement taken before the oral lesion existed, and its finding that the patients who developed mucositis had higher baseline anxiety and depression scores is the located reason the edge is ranked second and framed as direction-unresolved rather than authored as a consequence (PMID 38154442). The aphthous cross-sectional study is registered for the finding that ULCER SIZE AND RECURENCE FREQUENCY EXACERBATE DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS with reported regression coefficients, which is the only located evidence tying lesion burden to mood, and its different aetiology is disclosed (PMID 41234733). The second aphthous study is registered for its comparative design, reporting prevalence of extreme anxiety and depression against patients without the oral condition, and its very high anxiety figure is disclosed together with the fact that its comparison group is other patients rather than population norms (PMID 39036205). Because the prospective anchor points the opposite way, because the other two study a different aetiology, and because all three are small, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only with no rate for this identity.

THAT ANCHOR IS A SINGLE-CENTRE SAMPLE OF 37 INDIVIDUALS with a median age of 49, of whom roughly 38 PERCENT developed mucositis, so its baseline finding rests on a SMALL SUBGROUP and cannot be read as a general susceptibility finding (PMID 38154442). THE 66.1 PERCENT EXTREME-ANXIETY FIGURE IS EXTRAORDINARILY HIGH, is measured AGAINST PATIENTS WITHOUT THE ORAL CONDITION rather than against population norms, and comes from a study whose psychological analysis is presented as correlational (PMID 39036205). THE SECOND ANCHOR'S PREDICTORS INCLUDE DIETARY PREFERENCES and the use of traditional Chinese medicine interventions, which are behavioural and cultural variables that no located anchor controls for and that could confound the mood association. NO located anchor reports a depression DIAGNOSIS rate, a longitudinal mood course, any effect of treating the oral lesion on mood, or any mood outcome in a non-aphthous and non-treatment-induced form of this identity.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: A pre-existing mood disorder predating the oral disease, which the prospective anchor's baseline finding actively supports and which the cross-sectional anchors cannot exclude

A stress-mediated or immune-mediated susceptibility to developing the oral lesion, which the prospective anchor's baseline finding suggests is a real pathway and which would make mood a risk factor rather than a consequence

Adjustment to recurrent oral pain and to visible oral disease rather than a depressive disorder, which the located instruments do not separate and which is a different diagnosis with a different course

An eating-related avoidance syndrome, in which pain narrows diet and social eating and produces functional restriction that is scored on overlapping instruments, and which none of the located anchors measures directly

Comorbid systemic disease and its treatment, since both treatment-induced and aphthous forms occur in medically complex populations whose mental health is affected by the systemic illness independently of the oral lesion

governanceNotes: IDENTITY SCREEN, batch 87: AN ALIAS-SCOPE PROBLEM, NOT A DUPLICATION. The catalog alias 'oral mucositis' is a single string and does not name a second catalog identity, so nothing is duplicated, but it merges a general clinical concept with the distinct entity of cancer-therapy-induced mucositis. The catalog separately carries oral-candidiasis, oral-lichen-planus-lichenoid-lesions, gingivitis, periodontitis, periodontal-disease, oral-hairy-leukoplakia, erythroplakia, leukoplakia, xerostomia, glossitis, burning-mouth-syndrome and oral-cancer, none of which is an alias of this identity, so no identity-duplication closure is warranted. The alias tension is declared in the todo list so it is durable.

INCOMING-EDGE MAP, batch 87: this identity had ZERO registered incoming edges and ZERO registered outgoing edges before this batch, so both edges are new. Targets dysphagia at 17 and depressive-disorder at 94 are among the most heavily targeted identities in the registry.

TWO WITHHELD ROUTES, both on located evidence. (1) oral-candidiasis as CO-MANIFESTATION RATHER THAN CONSEQUENCE: the meta-analysis pools candidiasis at 24.11 percent in the same chemotherapy population as mucositis at 42.15 percent, and the located literature presents candidiasis as a concurrent oral consequence of the same impaired mucosal barrier rather than as a later secondary condition of the stomatitis, so the edge would have asserted a sequence the evidence does not support. (2) malnutrition as MISSING IDENTITY IN THE CATALOG'S TERMS: the located evidence addresses reduced oral intake, nutritional support and weight trajectory, but the corresponding catalog identities were not located in this batch's screen and the route is therefore recorded rather than forced onto a wrong target.

AN INTERNAL NULL CARRIED ON THE DYSPHAGIA EDGE: the strongest anchor found the dysphagia association significant for chemotherapy-induced mucositis and NOT significant for radiotherapy-induced mucositis, adjusted odds ratio 1.21 (95% CI 0.84 to 1.77), on the same adjusted model. The null is stated on the face of the edge and is the reason the agent class is a mandatory field on any claim.

A DISPARITY FINDING REGISTERED ON THE DYSPHAGIA EDGE: the same national-data study reports that mucositis outcomes disproportionately affect females, Black, Hispanic and Medicaid patients and those with lower incomes. This is recorded on the edge because an association that falls unequally is an association that must not be presented as uniform.
